name_en: Yakiniku — bite-size beef and offal grilled at the table and dipped in sauce
summary_ja: 牛の正肉や内臓を一口大に切り、卓上の網や鉄板で客が自ら焼いて、タレや塩で食べる料理。朝鮮半島の肉料理を下敷きに、戦後、在日コリアンの営む店が内臓肉を焼いて出したことから広がったとされ、焼いた後でつけダレにくぐらせる食べ方など、日本で形が整ったという。
summary_en: Bite-size beef and offal that diners grill themselves over a tabletop grate or griddle, then dip in sauce or eat with salt. Rooted in Korean meat cookery, it is said to have spread after the war from restaurants run by Korean residents of Japan that grilled offal, and to have taken its Japanese shape, such as dipping the meat after grilling, along the way.
source_publisher: 一般社団法人全国焼肉協会
